requirements.note: Inset-grouped list sectioned by month, newest first; each row shows name, date (no year), exercise count and volume (e.g. 6,767.5 lb), all correct.
Detail shows a summary (date, exercises, sets, total volume), then one section per exercise with Set n / weight × reps and a per-exercise volume footer. Exercise rows push to the exercise screen.

Name field, Add Exercise sheet with system search bar and a muscle pop-up menu (works with search), one exercise per trip. Add Set sheet uses number pads, is pre-filled with the previous set and checks input ('Weight is a number of pounds from 0 to 2,000', Save disabled). Tapping a set edits it, swipe left deletes it. Finish asks for confirmation and the workout appears at the top of History with the correct volume (135.5×12 = 1,626 lb). Discard asks for confirmation.
Library tab with a large title, grouped by muscle with section headers, rows push to the exercise screen. No search on this screen (not required).
Shows the best set (135.5 lb × 12, with workout and date), muscle, equipment and 'Workouts (2)' listing each with its top weight; rows push to the workout.
A workout in progress (name, exercise, sets, after editing and deleting a set) was restored exactly after relaunch; a finished workout stayed in History after relaunch.

tells: The Add/Edit Set sheet has a hand-drawn header instead of a navigation bar: a blue X and a grey check circle, a title in a larger font than system sheet titles, and no grabber.
At the largest text size that custom header grows to two lines and covers the 'Exercise · Set 1' subtitle beneath it.
Only one exercise can be added per trip into the picker; the sheet closes after each pick.
The muscle filter is a pop-up menu in a form row rather than a scope bar; it is native, but slower to switch than a segmented or scope control.
Dates in History omit the year (fine within this year, but older entries depend on the section header).
A.scroll: History (8 pages) and Library scroll and fling smoothly with sticky month and muscle headers. No blank rows or pop-in, the large title collapses correctly, and scroll position is kept after pushing a workout and coming back.

requirements.note: Inset-grouped list sectioned by month, newest first; rows show name, full date with year, and SF Symbol icons with exercise count and volume, all correct.

Summary section (long-form date, exercises, sets, total volume), then per-exercise sections with numbered sets showing weight × reps and per-set volume, plus a volume footer. Exercise rows push to the exercise screen.

A start screen asks for the name. The Add Exercises sheet has a system search field, horizontally scrolling muscle chips, multi-select with check circles and an 'Add (2)' button. Each added exercise shows its previous best. The Add Set sheet uses a native navigation bar with grabber, number pads plus steppers (reps ±1, weight ±2.5), is pre-filled from the last logged set, and shows a live volume. Tapping a set opens Edit Set, which has a Delete Set button; swipe-to-delete also works. Finish shows a popover confirmation that warns exercises without sets will be left out, and the workout appears in History (25×10 = 250 lb).
Library tab grouped by muscle, with headers like 'Arms (20)', a search field, and each row's workout count.
Shows muscle, equipment, the best set with a trophy (heaviest weight, tappable to its workout) and 'Workouts (2)' with sets and top set for each.
A workout in progress (name, exercises, edited and deleted sets) was restored after relaunch, and the app reopens on the Workout tab; finished workouts persist in History.

bugs: On the 'Ready to train?' start screen, the keyboard covers the in-list 'Start Workout' button and the list does not scroll to reveal it; a tap there lands on the keyboard. The 'Start' button in the navigation bar still works.
tells: The muscle filter chips are a hand-drawn row of capsule buttons rather than a system scope bar or segmented control.
The exercise screen opens with the workout you came from shown as selected (a grey highlight that stays), which looks like a stuck selection.
The Library tab uses a small inline title while History and Workout use large titles.
Starting a workout takes an extra step (a 'Ready to train?' screen with its own Start button) before you can add exercises.
B.scroll: History (about 10 pages) and the 120-row Library scroll and fling smoothly with no blank or popping rows, and the large title collapses normally. Scroll position is kept after a push and back, and pulling past the top bounces normally.

why: Both apps are clean, native-looking and meet every requirement. B goes further where it matters while logging: a multi-select exercise picker, steppers with pre-filled values and live volume in a proper system sheet, previous bests shown in the workout, and library search with workout counts. A's custom set-entry header is its most visible tell and overlaps text at large sizes, while B's flaws (a stuck row highlight and a start button hidden by the keyboard) are smaller.
